verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI documents function tools registered with the `@agent.tool` decorator, and agents that contain tools and are generic in their dependency and output types (`Agent[Foobar, list[str]]`). Community users independently say it makes constructing an agent very easy and tool-calling frictionless. missing for 10: explicit evidence that tool parameter type hints are turned into validated schemas, and a concrete few-lines code example in the pack.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define an agent with typed custom tools in a few lines of code

citations.quote: @agent.tool is considered the default decorator since in the majority of cases tools will need access to the agent context.
Function tools provide a mechanism for models to perform actions and retrieve extra information to help them generate a response.
In typing terms, agents are generic in their dependency and output types...your IDE can tell you when you have the right type
It does make constructing any given agent very easy
